goal: zig-regex can compile patterns over raw bytes instead of UTF-8 text, which ClamAV PCRE subsignatures, YARA regex strings and zig-waf @rx on binary bodies all need.
scope: A `bytes` compile option
In bytes mode `\xHH` is one byte (today parseHexEscape turns it into the code point's UTF-8 bytes)
`.` matches any byte, and with dotall also newline
Character classes are byte sets with no UTF-8 range decomposition; case-insensitive folds ASCII only
Unicode properties are rejected in bytes mode with a clear error
Tests for every construct in both modes
notes: Default behaviour stays UTF-8 so existing users see no change
PCRE byte semantics are the reference; the differential experiment comes later in zig-anti-virus (P4.19)
accept: `\x80\xff` matches exactly those two bytes in bytes mode
Every existing test still passes
New tests cover classes, dot, case folding and anchors in bytes mode

goal: A matcher that never allocates during a match: the caller passes scratch memory once and reuses it, so the scan hot path in zig-anti-virus and zig-waf stays allocation-free.
scope: A `Scratch` type sized from the compiled program, created once per thread
`isMatch`, `find` and `findAll` variants taking the scratch and no allocator
The lazy DFA's mutable state moves into the scratch, so one compiled program is shared read-only across threads
Benchmarks before and after
notes: The LazyDfa is mutable per matcher today; moving it to scratch is what makes a shared, read-only program possible
A test allocator that fails on any allocation must pass the matching tests
accept: Matching with a failing allocator passes the full test suite
Throughput does not regress on the existing benchmarks

goal: Callers can bound how much memory and time one match may use, so hostile input cannot blow up a scan: a configurable lazy-DFA state cap and a per-match step budget.
scope: Configurable DFA state cap (fixed at 16384 today, up to about 16 MiB per regex per thread); zig-anti-virus wants about 256
When the cap is hit, fall back to the NFA without failing
Per-match step budget for the backtracker (10M default today) and the NFA, returning a distinct `BudgetExceeded` result
Tests with pathological patterns
notes: BudgetExceeded must never be reported as no match; zig-anti-virus records it as a limit event
accept: With a 256-state cap, scratch memory per regex stays under a documented bound
A catastrophic pattern returns BudgetExceeded within the configured steps

goal: An API that tells the caller which literal strings every match must contain, so prefilters (zig-anti-virus atoms, zig-waf phrase sets) can skip regex evaluation entirely when no required literal is present.
scope: Public function returning required literal factors: prefix, suffix and inner factors, each with whether it is case-folded
Works in UTF-8 and bytes mode
Returns none when no factor of at least a minimum length exists
Tests with alternation, optional parts and repetition
out_of_scope: The literal matchers themselves (P2.06 to P2.08)
notes: The optimizer already computes literal_prefix and required_literal internally; this exposes and extends them to sets of factors
accept: `foo(bar|baz)qux` reports `foo` and `qux` as required
`(a|b)*` reports nothing
Bytes-mode factors match raw bytes

goal: Compiled regex programs can be written into a file and loaded later without allocation, so zig-anti-virus stores PCRE and YARA regexes inside its mmapped signature database instead of compiling them at startup.
scope: Serialise a compiled program to a relocatable byte blob: offsets, not pointers, little-endian, versioned
Load from a borrowed slice (for example an mmapped region) with no allocation and validation of bounds
Round-trip tests and a fuzz target for the loader
notes: Until this exists zig-anti-virus keeps a bounded runtime compile cache of about 4 MB
accept: Every test pattern matches identically after a round trip

goal: A fast multi-literal search for small pattern sets (up to a few dozen literals), the Teddy algorithm with SIMD nibble tables, as the first piece of a literals module shared by zig-anti-virus and zig-waf.
scope: src/literals/teddy.zig: build from up to 64 literals, SIMD scan using @Vector on x86_64 and aarch64, verification of candidates
Reports literal id and offset
Case-insensitive option for ASCII
Benchmark against a naive multi-memmem
notes: Zig has no runtime-index byte shuffle builtin, so the nibble lookup needs inline assembly (pshufb, tbl) behind a small wrapper
Used by zig-anti-virus for small target-type partitions
accept: Exhaustive tests against naive search on random inputs
At least 5 GB/s on 8 literals on a modern core, measured and recorded

goal: A binary-safe Aho-Corasick automaton with pattern ids, optional case folding and a relocatable serialised form, replacing the ASCII-only matcher in zig-waf and serving large literal sets everywhere.
scope: src/literals/aho_corasick.zig: build from any byte strings, report (pattern id, start, end) for every match, leftmost-longest and all-matches modes
Dense root table and compact transitions; option for a full DFA when the automaton is small
Case-folding option instead of always lowercasing
Serialise to a relocatable blob and run from a borrowed slice without allocation
notes: phrase.zig lowercases every byte, binary-searches edges per node, and returns only start and end, not which pattern matched. That makes it unusable for signatures
For very large sets the sampled Bloom prefilter (P2.08) is expected to beat this; the bake-off in zig-anti-virus decides (P4.16)
accept: Exhaustive differential tests against naive search including bytes 0x00 and 0xff
Serialised automaton matches identically after loading

goal: A sampled split-block Bloom prefilter for very large literal sets: positions are probed independently with no loop-carried state, so the CPU keeps many memory loads in flight. This is the core of zig-anti-virus pattern matching.
scope: src/literals/sbbf.zig: 32-byte split blocks with 8 words, hash of a 4-byte gram with a seed, 8 bit positions from odd multipliers
Stride tiers: a literal with a long anchor inserts all grams at offsets 0 to s-1 so sampling every s-th position never misses it
Probe kernel that hashes 16 overlapping grams from one vector, then scalar block tests; candidates written to a ring branch-free
Builder sized to a target bits-per-key, serialised relocatably
out_of_scope: Atom selection and tiers A to D policy (zig-anti-virus P4.03)
notes: Do not use gathers: they are slow on Intel parts with the Downfall microcode mitigation
About 16 bits per key gives roughly 0.1 to 0.3 percent false positives
Per-byte cost estimate: about 0.6 cycles for stride 8, 1.2 for stride 4, 4.5 for stride 1 [E], measured in P2.09
accept: Never a false negative on randomized tests with strides 1, 4 and 8
False-positive rate within 20 percent of the theoretical rate for the configured size

goal: A streaming MIME walker that processes a message chunk by chunk with bounded memory, finds boundaries with SIMD, and walks nested multiparts, so mail scanning never buffers whole messages.

notes: The mail parser's MultipartParser takes the whole body, is not recursive and allocates per part; the streaming parser buffers all headers and only handles the top level. This replaces both for scanning

goal: Real numbers about the ClamAV databases replace every estimate in the design: how many signatures of each kind, how long their fixed runs are, how many hashes have no size, and how densely sizes are covered.
scope: A `zav census` subcommand or script that reads main.cvd and daily.cvd (fetched by the host, never committed)
Counts by file extension, target type, offset kind and functionality level
Longest fixed run per subsignature, as a histogram over tiers A (11+ bytes), B (7-10), C (4-6), D (3 or fewer)
Size-less hash signature count per algorithm; distinct sizes per table; coverage of sizes below 2^24
Signature name tokenisation ratio; PCRE subsignature count
Results committed as docs/CENSUS.md with the database versions
notes: Size-less hashes force hashing every file and are the main threat to hash skipping; the count decides mitigations
Tier D counts size the candidate-storm risk for E3
accept: docs/CENSUS.md lists every count above with database versions
Rerunning the census on the same databases gives identical numbers

goal: zav reads ClamAV database files directly and verifies they are genuine, so a host can compile its own database from the files it downloads.
scope: src/compile/cvd.zig: parse the 512-byte header (build time, version, signature count, functionality level, MD5, digital signature, builder)
Stream the tar.gz body with std.compress.flate and std.tar; detect plain-tar CLD files by magic
Verify the MD5 and the digital signature (and the external .sign file on newer releases); refuse unverified input unless an explicit flag is passed for local testing
Yield each contained file to the per-extension parsers
notes: Databases are fetched by each host and compiled locally; they are never committed or re-hosted
The header field list is pieced together from docs and libclamav source; test against real files
accept: Current main.cvd and daily.cvd parse and verify
A file with one flipped byte fails verification
Fuzz target for the header and archive reader

goal: Hash signatures from every ClamAV hash format load into one rule IR, the input to the hash index.
scope: src/compile/ir.zig: rule representation with source, name tokens, functionality level range and flags
Parsers: .hdb (MD5:size:name), .hsb (hash:size:name with MD5, SHA1 or SHA256 by length, `*` size with functionality level 73+), .mdb and .msb (PE section size:hash:name), .imp (import hash)
PUA variants with the u prefix
Every rejected line recorded with a reason for the coverage report
accept: Every hash line in current main and daily parses or is recorded with a reason
Unit tests for each format including malformed lines

goal: Allowlists, ignore lists and functionality levels are applied at compile time, and the compiler writes a coverage report that counts every signature it could not include and why.
scope: .ign2 drops signatures by name at compile time, so ignoring costs nothing at scan time
.fp and .sfp stored as full-digest allowlist tables consulted after a detection
Functionality-level filtering with the engine's declared level
Coverage report section in the compiled database and as text: counts skipped by reason (unsupported format, target, feature, bytecode)
notes: Allowlist digests are never truncated: a 64-bit prefix would let someone forge an allowlisted file with about 2^64 work
Bytecode (.cbc) is out of scope; its signatures appear in the report as skipped
accept: `zav coverage` prints the report for a compiled database
A signature listed in .ign2 does not appear in the compiled output

goal: The compiled database format: one signed, versioned, offset-only blob that the daemon maps read-only, so signatures cost no private memory and loading takes milliseconds.
scope: src/db/format.zig: 4 KiB header (magic, versions, feature flags, database version, source versions, BLAKE3 root, key id, ed25519 signature), section table with xxh3 per section
extern structs with comptime size and alignment asserts; little-endian; offsets relative to sections
src/db/writer.zig: write to a temp file, fsync, rename
src/db/reader.zig: raw posix.mmap(PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE), header and section-table checks, hard failure if mmap fails
Full BLAKE3 verification once at install, recorded in a sidecar keyed by device, inode, size and mtime
Hot region first and 2 MiB aligned
notes: Never use std.Io.File.MemoryMap for the database: it silently falls back to allocate plus read, which would turn about 200 MB of signatures into private memory
Big-endian hosts are refused
accept: Open and validate a 200 MB test blob in under 10 ms with a warm page cache
Any flipped byte in the header or a section is detected by the right check
Private dirty memory after opening is under 1 MB

goal: A hash index that decides from the file size alone whether any hashing is needed, keeps only 8 bytes per signature hot, and confirms every hit against the full digest.
scope: Need map: 4 bits per size (MD5, SHA1, SHA256) for sizes below 2^24, sorted overflow list above, a global size-less mask
Per table (algorithm and kind): sorted distinct sizes, a radix index for two-probe size lookup, 8-byte digest prefixes sorted within each size bucket
Cold section with full digests and signature ids, read only on a prefix hit
Size-less tables searched by interpolation over prefixes
Signature names stored as tokens, about 16 bytes per record, rebuilt only when a result is reported
External merge sort in the compiler so building fits in about 128 MB
out_of_scope: Optional binary-fuse filter, decided by E1 (P3.09)
notes: About 32 MB of clean mapped memory for 4M entries [E]
A prefix collision can never cause a detection: the full digest is always compared
accept: Every hash signature in main and daily is found by lookup with its correct name
Random non-signature digests produce zero false matches over 100M lookups
Warm lookup under 300 ns

goal: Hashing runs in one pass that computes only the algorithms a file needs, using hardware SHA instructions whenever the CPU has them, even from a single distributed binary.
scope: src/hash/multihash.zig: update any subset of MD5, SHA1 and SHA256 over the same cache-resident block
CPU-variant objects (x86-64-v2, v3, v3 plus sha, aarch64 plus crypto) selected at runtime through cpuid or sysctl
Hardware SHA-1 kernels for x86 SHA-NI and ARMv8, which std lacks
Speculative hashing for streams of unknown size, dropped once the size passes the largest signature size for that table
notes: std.crypto uses SHA-NI or ARMv8 sha256h only when the target enables them at comptime, so a baseline build silently falls back to software
MD5 is inherently serial at about 600 to 700 MB/s per core
accept: Digests match std and reference vectors for every variant
Runtime dispatch picks the hardware path on a CPU that has it, verified in a test

goal: E1: measure what the hash index costs and how much hashing it avoids, and decide whether a binary-fuse filter is worth adding.
scope: Lookup cost with 4M plus 1M entries, warm and cold page cache
Share of bytes and files that skip each algorithm on a benign filesystem corpus and a large-file corpus
Optional binary-fuse filter (about 9 bits per key) measured against plain interpolation search
Results added to docs/DESIGN.md
notes: Pass line: warm lookup at most 300 ns and at least 70 percent of MD5 bytes skipped on the benign corpus [E]. If missed: add the filter or rework the size map
accept: Numbers recorded with hardware and corpus identifiers
A decision on the filter written in the issue and in docs/DESIGN.md

goal: E8: measure the hashers on baseline and native builds, so the engine knows what size gating saves and whether the variant dispatch is worth it.
scope: Throughput of MD5, SHA1 and SHA256 on baseline x86_64, the sha variant, and aarch64 with crypto
Overhead of runtime dispatch
Results added to docs/DESIGN.md
notes: Pass line: SHA256 at least 1.5 GB/s and SHA1 at least 2 GB/s with hardware. If missed: keep software paths and lean on size gating
accept: Numbers recorded for each variant and CPU tested

goal: Hosts that have a MalwareBazaar key can add its SHA-256 hash feed to their compiled database. It stays off by default because of the feed's terms.
scope: Import the MalwareBazaar CSV export (sha256 and file size) into the SHA-256 whole-file table with its own source id
Size-keyed like the ClamAV tables, so it benefits from the need map
Configuration takes the auth key from the environment; nothing is fetched without it
Documentation states the not-for-profit terms and that the data must not be redistributed
notes: Every MalwareBazaar export now needs an auth key; downloads without one fail
Terms limit free use to not-for-profit purposes and forbid derivative works and training models
accept: A sample export imports and its hashes are detected
With no key configured, no network request is made

goal: The scan core's shared building blocks: a Source type every parser reads from, per-thread scratch arenas, and the limits that keep hostile files from exhausting time or memory.
scope: src/engine/source.zig: file descriptor range, memory slice, decompressor over a parent source, spill file; sequential and positional reads
src/engine/scratch.zig: per-worker arena reserved as virtual memory, faulted in lazily, trimmed with madvise after idle
src/engine/limits.zig: max scan size, file size, recursion (17), files, embedded executables, normaliser sizes, per-member ratio and output caps, total output budget
src/engine/budget.zig: global big-window budget (64 MiB default) for decoder windows over 1 MiB
Limit events reported as results, never silent passes
notes: No allocation in the hot loop: everything a scan needs comes from scratch
Defaults match clamd so verdicts are comparable
accept: A test scan of a file performs zero heap allocations after scratch creation
Exceeding each limit yields the matching limit event

goal: The zav command line exists with its first commands, so every later feature has a place to be exercised by hand and in tests.
scope: src/cli/main.zig on zig-cli
`zav compile <sources...> -o db.zavdb`, `zav info <db>`, `zav coverage <db>`, `zav scan <paths...> --db <db>`
`--json` output on every command; exit code 0 clean, 1 infected, 2 error
Help text and a man-page style docs/CLI.md
out_of_scope: host, audit, daemon, update and bench commands (later phases)
accept: Each command runs and has a test
Exit codes match the documented values

goal: The first end-to-end scan: compile a database, open it, scan a file, report a detection. EICAR is built in so every install can prove it works.
scope: Built-in EICAR test signature, always present, reported as `Eicar-Test-Signature`
Scan path: open, stat, need-map check, fused hash, index lookup, allowlist check, result
EICAR test files (plain and the two zipped variants) generated in tests, never committed as raw files
Integration test compiling hash signatures from a fixture and scanning fixtures
out_of_scope: Zipped EICAR detection needs the zip parser (P5.03); the zipped variants are marked pending until then
notes: EICAR must start the file, may be followed only by whitespace, and the file must be 128 bytes or less
accept: `zav scan eicar.com` exits 1 and names Eicar-Test-Signature
A clean file exits 0
Integration test green in CI

goal: Phase gate: every ClamAV hash signature compiles into a database the engine maps read-only, and raw files scan against it with the expected verdicts and memory.
scope: Compile current main and daily hash signatures with the coverage report
Scan a benign corpus and a set of known-hash samples (by hash manifest, run isolated)
Measure private dirty memory of `zav scan` with the full hash database loaded
Update docs/DESIGN.md with census, E1 and E8 results
notes: Gate for P3; the census (P3.02), E1 (P3.09) and E8 (P3.10) must be closed first
accept: All hash signatures compile, the coverage report shows only expected skips
Every known-hash sample is detected with the right name and no benign file is
Private dirty under 24 MB with the hash database loaded
